2. The opposite party as plaintiff instituted the instant Admiralty suit on 3-3-2011 impleading the vessel MV Yu Fu and its owners and parties interested in the said vessel as defendants and praying for a decree for realization of outstanding amount US $ 1,34,814.78 equivalent to Bangladeshi Taka 94,37,034.06 for the loss and damages suffered by the plaintiff till 24-2-2011 for supply of bunkers payable to the plaintiff due to breach of contract and further for pendent lite interest. 

 3. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the plaintiff is a company incorporated in the United States of America and has been engaged in the business of supplying marine fuel and lubricant to marine vessels; that the defendant vessel MV Yu Fu arrived at Chittagong Port at 13-30 hours on 23-2-2011 carrying Refined Palm Oil (RPO); that the defendant vessel was renamed twice since 22-4-2005 pursuant to transfer of its ownerships; that in the course of its business, the plaintiff supplied bunkers to the vessel MV Aral Wind between 20-5-2009 and 9-6-2009 under two separate contracts, both governed by the plaintiffs "Standard Terms and Conditions for The Sale of Marine Bunker Fuels and Lubricants" as expressly provided in the said contracts; that both the contracts dated 18-5-2009 and 5-6-2009 contained reference to the Standard Terms and Conditions of the plaintiff in the following manner. 

 that the Standard Terms and Conditions for the Sale of Marine Bunker Fuels and Lubricants, which were provided by the plaintiff to the defendant prior to entering the contracts, contained the following clause: 

 4. In pursuant to the above provisions of contracts dated 18-5-2009 and 5-6-2009 and the Standard Terms and Conditions for The Sale of Marine Bunker Fuels and Lubricants, a maritime lien exists on the defendant's vessel; that the plaintiff as seller issued commercial invoices in favour of the defendant-vessel in respect of the aforesaid supply of bunkers which is described in paragraph No. 7 of the plaint; that the said commercial invoices remained out-standing upon expiry of the due date for payment and remain outstanding till date; that on 9-9-2009, Aral Wind Limited transferred owner-ships of the defendant vessel to North Oil Project Limited and the vessel was renamed MV Zaral. On 3-1-2009, North Oil Project Limited transferred the ownership of the vessel to Target Shipping Limited and the vessel was named again as MV Yu Fu and has been registered under the Hong Kong flag; that as a result of the defendant's vessel failure to pay for the outstanding amount for supply of bunkers at the due date as provided in the aforesaid commercial invoices, the plaintiff has suffered loss and damages to the extent of US$ 1,34,814.78 till 24-2-2011; that the plaintiff reserve the right to seek further damages if caused by the defendant vessel's inability to pay for the amount outstanding in the future. The heads of loss and damages are described in the body of the plaint and the total amount of claim now stands at US $ 1,34,814.78 equivalent of Taka 94,37,034.60 (Taka Ninety Four Lac and thirty seven thou-sand and thirty four) only calculated at the rate of US $ 1.00 equivalent to Taka 70.00 as prevailing on the date of filing of the suit; that the plaintiff reserves the right to modify its claim after assessment of the total loss suffered by them due to interalia, further interest accrued on the principal amount etc, if any. The plaintiff instituted the present this suit by invoking the jurisdiction of this court in respect of its claim mentioned in section ৩(২)(ঠ) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 for loss and damages suffered by it for supply of necessaries or materials to the defendant vessel for her operation and maintenance. 

 5. The defendants entered appearance in the suit on 30-5-2011 and prayed for time for filing written statement. It appears that the defendant filed the present application on 6-6-2011 for return of the plaint and on the same day defendant also filed an application for dismissal of the suit for lack of Admiralty Jurisdiction over the said vessel, but in the cause title of the said application it was mistakenly written "The written objection of the first instant suit." It further appears that both the applications are pending for long time but the defendants did not take any step for hearing of the said applications till 16-10-2011. Subsequently, on the prayer of the learned Advocate of the defendants, Mr Muhammad Salahuddin, the suit was fixed on 2-6-2013 for hearing of the said application. The defendants took several adjournments during the period of 28-5-2011 upto 7-7-2013 for hearing of the application and for filing written statement. Then the suit was again fixed on 14-7-2013 for hearing of the said application dated 6-6-2011 and filing written statement but the defendants without filing any written statement, filed an application on 6-6-2013 for amendment of the application dated 6-6-2011 for return of the plaint/dismissal of the suit. It also appears that the defendant-applicants earlier filed two application dated 14-8-2011 and 29-5-2013 for return of the plaint and to discharge the bank guarantee by supplying copy of those applications to the learned Advocate for the plaintiff but those were not pressed. 

 7. The defendant Nos. 1-3 as applicants in their application for return of the plaint dated 6-6-2011 and for amendment of the same by application dated 6-6-2013 (as referred to as the application) stated that the suit is not maintainable in the manner and capacity it has proceeded in so far. The instant suit was filed against the claim for supply of bunkers to the vessel MV Aral Wind subsequently, renamed MV Yu Fu under ownership of M/s. Target Shipping Limited at the time of bringing up the action, M/s Aral Wind Limited has no beneficial ownership over all the shares of the ship MV Yu Fu which was admitted by the plaintiff in paragraph No. 4 of the suit. It was further stated that the claim against the supply of bunkers constitutes a maritime lien and refers to contract stipulating the terms and conditions of such supply of bunkers to MV Aral Wind. Such claim of maritime lien against supply of bunkers is not maintainable. It is also stated that in exercising such claim a true maritime lien must be in order for the lien to travel with the vessel. The doctrine of a maritime lien cannot be established by mere contractual arrangement but stipulation imposed by relevant statutes and laws must be considered. Maritime lien cannot be created by agreement between the parties under sections 477-479 of the Bangladesh Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 1983 which governs the doctrine of maritime lien, such a claim against unpaid bunkers can-not be considered as a maritime lien. Thus the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh cannot invoke admiralty jurisdiction of the instant matter of the maritime lien. That this court arrested the vessel MV Yu Fu on 3-3-2011 with the expectation of a successful establishment of a potential maritime lien over the vessel MV Yu Fu by the plaintiff. However, such a claim of maritime lien cannot be established under sections 477-479 of the Bangladesh Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 1983 read with section 4(3) and other corresponding provisions of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000. Thus exercise of the admiralty jurisdiction over the vessel and arrest order against the said vessel may be vacated. Accordingly, the defendants prayed for return of the plaint, dismissing the suit of the maritime lien claim in rem set up in the suit is not amenable to the admiralty jurisdiction of this Hon'ble court. 

 8. In their written objection dated 3-7-2013 to the application for return of the plaint, the plaintiff stated that the application for return of the plaint is misconceived and is not maintainable inasmuch as the plaintiff has a maritime lien against the vessel MV Yu Fu (Former Aral Wind) as set out in the plaint of the instant suit as prima-facie established by the plaintiff. According to section 4(3) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 (shortly, the Ain, 2000), the Hon'ble High Court Division is empowered to exercise its jurisdiction in respect of the subject matter of the instant suit. It was further stated that the plaintiff supplied bunker to MV Yu Fu when it had the name MV Aral Wind between 20-5-2009 and 9-6-2009 but no payment has been received for the said bunkers till date. That the claim of maritime lien is not premised on the beneficial ownership of the vessel. A maritime lien adheres to the ship from the time of the events giving rise to the maritime lien, and then continues to be binding on the vessel until the lien is dis-charged under the law and is not extinguished by the sale of a vessel to a bonafide purchaser for value without notice of the claim. It also stated that under section 4(3) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000, the admiralty jurisdiction of Hon'ble High Court Division may be exercised in rem where the amount claimed relates to any ship, aircraft or other property over which there is a maritime lien or other charge. Therefore, Maritime lien arose in the present suit when bunkers was supplied as per contract dated 18-5-2009 and 5-6-2009 as are governed by the Standard Terms and Conditions which are agreed and acknowledged by both the parties as maritime lien over the vessel. 

 9. Section 4(3) of the Ain, 2000 clearly provides that the amount of claim relates to any ship, aircraft or other property over which there is a maritime lien or other charge, the admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court Division as the Court of Admiralty may in such case be exercised by an action in rem against that ship, air-craft or property. Thus the present suit is clearly maintainable in this Admiralty Court. Accordingly, the plaintiff prayed for rejection of the defendant's application for return of the plaint. 

 10. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed, with Mr Muhammad Salahuddin, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1-3 submits that the present suit set-ting up a maritime claim is not amenable to the Admiralty Jurisdiction in rem of this Hon'ble Court. He further submits that the plaintiff brought the instant suit before this Hon'ble Court falls under section ৩(২)(ঠ) of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000 that is any claims in respect of goods or materials supplied to a ship for her operation and maintenance. 

 15. In reply to the above submissions, Dr Sharif Bhuiyan, with Mr Tanim Hussain Showan, the learned Advocates appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party submits that the instant claim made by the plaintiff covered under section 3(2)(ঠ) and the suit instituted by the plaintiff under the admiralty jurisdiction is maintainable. He next submits that section 4(3) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 (shortly, the Ain) which clearly provides that where the amount claimed relates to any ship, aircraft or other property over which there is a maritime lien or other charge, the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court Division as the court of admiralty may in such a case exercise an action in rem against that ship, aircraft or property. Since the plaintiff's claim is a claim arising from maritime lien against the defendant vessel, section 4(3) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 empowers this court to exercise its jurisdiction in rem against the defendant vessel. This court has jurisdiction to adjudicate the instant suit based on maritime lien pursuant to its statutory jurisdiction under the Ain. He further submits that there is no provision in the said Ain to the effect that maritime lien referred to in the Ain would be confined to maritime lien arising under the Bangladesh Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 1983. He also submits that the contracts dated 18-5-2009 and 5-6-2009 under which the plaintiff had supplied bunkers to the defendant vessel incorporated by reference the Standard Terms and Conditions for Sale of Marine Bunker Fuels and Lubricants states the following terms: 

 17. In reply to the submission of the learned Advocate for the defendants-applicants to the effect that the existence of the maritime lien should be determined according to the 'lex fori' is erroneous inasmuch as the 'lex fori' only determines the procedure and not for claiming the substantive rights. The plaintiff has filed the instant suit in accordance with the procedural laws of Bangladesh. The question of whether or not a maritime lien exists is a question of substantive right and not a question of procedure. He further submits that the decisions of US case of Bominflot Inc. vs The MV Henrich S cited by the learned Advocate for the defendants also supports the principle that an express choice of law clause is conclusive and should be given effect by the courts. His further contention is that existence of maritime lien entitles the plaintiff to enforce its claim against any third party in possession of the vessel. A maritime lien is an invisible, secret, indelible or inalienable encumbrance. Once it attaches to a res a maritime lien thereafter "travels with the thing into whosever possession it may come". In support of his contentions Mr Sharif, the learned Advocate has referred to the case of Bangladesh Air Service (Pvt.) Limited vs British Airways PLC ??? 187, In the case of Trans-Tec Asia vs MV Harmony Container 518 F.3d 1120 (9th Circuit, 2008) and the case of Bold Buccleugh (1851) PC 267, Kolarado (1923) Rep 531 and 34 DLR (AD) 110 in the case of Al-Sayer Navigation Co. vs Delta International Traders Ltd. 

 19. The plaintiff instituted the present Admiralty Suit in rem along with an application for arrest of the defendant No. 1 vessel MV Yu Fu (call sign-VRGD8, IMO-8517035). This court has arrested the vessel MV Yu Fu on 3-3-2011 with an order to furnish security in order to get the release of the vessel, accordingly, the defendant Nos. 1-3 furnished security in the form of Bank guarantee for an amount of US$ 1,34,814.78 issued by the Standard Chartered Bank, Dhaka and the vessel was released from arrest by order dated 15-3-2011. 

 21. I will first of all take up the legal contentions advanced by the learned Advocate for the defendants in support of this application for return of the plaint. Learned Advocate for the defendants-applicants submits that the claim of the plaintiff as disclosed in the plaint does not fall under any of the subsection (3) of section 4 of the Ain and setting up a maritime claim in action in rem is not amenable/maintainable under the Admiralty Jurisdiction and thus the plaint should be returned to the plaintiff. The plaintiff has relied on clause (a) of subsection (2) of section 3 and sub-section (3) of section 4 of the said Ain, 2000 to contend that the suit filed by it under the Admiralty Jurisdiction of this court is maintainable. 

 23. It is not disputed rather admitted that the contract dated 18-5-2009 and 5-6-2009 under which the plaintiff supplied bunkers to the defendant-vessel, MV Yu Fu (former MV Arial Wind) incorporated by reference to the Standard Terms and Conditions for Supply of Bunkers which include expressly "Sellers Maritime Liens Rights". 

 25. The next legal objection of the learned counsel for the defendants is that the claim of the plaintiffs is based on clause 0) of subsection (2) of section 3 of the said Ain, while section 4(2) of the said Ain provides only in respect of claim arising under clauses (ক) to (গ), and (দ) of sub-section (2) of section 3 of the said Ain, an action in rem would lie under the Admiralty jurisdiction of this court and not in respect of claim mentioned in section 3(2)(ঠ). It is accordingly contended that by necessary implication, filing of a suit in rem in respect of claim falling under clause (ঠ) of section 3 (2) of the Ain shall be deemed to have been prohibited. Subsection (2) of section 4 of the Ain relied by the learned counsel for the defendants which reads as follows:- 

 29. Learned Advocate for the defendant submits that as the claim of the plaintiff against the supply of bunkers to the vessel MV Arial Wind (now MV Yu Fu) under the ownership of M/s Target Shipping Limited but at the time of initiation /filing of the suit M/s Arial Wind Limited has no beneficial ownership over all the shares of the vessel MV Yu Fu and the claim in the present suit is not recognized as subject to maritime lien and section 4(4) of the Ain has no manner of application, therefore, the suit filed by the plaintiff is not covered under the above referred clause of subsection (2) of section 3 of the Ain, 2000. 

 32. It cannot be denied that the Admiralty Court in Bangladesh prior to the enforcement of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 (Act XLIII of 2000) were exercising admiralty jurisdiction in order to enforce the maritime lien and, therefore, by virtue of the above proviso, the above jurisdiction remained intact apart from the express jurisdiction conferred on the High Court under the Ain by subsection (3) of section 4 of the Ain, which provides that admiralty jurisdiction can be exercised in any case, in which, there is a maritime lien. Thus the plaintiff's claim arising from maritime lien against the defendant vessel prima-facie fall under section 4(3) of the said Ain. 

 34. This court notice that the dispute as has been brought before this court has arisen from the supply of bunkers by the plaintiff to the defendant vessel and arising out of the contract and therefore squarely falls under clause (ঠ) of subsection (2) of section 3 and has locus-standi to invoke the jurisdiction under the provision of subsection (3) and (4) of section 4 the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 and is clearly maintainable in this Admiralty Court. 

 35. It may be mentioned here that in order to ascertain whether the jurisdiction of the court exist with relation to the claim of the plaintiff the same is to be examined with reference to the allegations and averments made in the plaint. On a primary examination of the averments made in the plaint I am satisfied that prima-facie, the claim of the plaintiff is maintainable under the admiralty jurisdiction of this court. A deeper and full appreciation of these contentions is not possible at this stage of hearing which could only be undertaken at the trial of the suit when all the evidence will be available before the court. In the premises above I am not inclined to accept the contention of the defendants that the plaintiffs cannot present the admiralty suit. 

 36. The learned Advocate appearing from both the sides referred good number of decisions at the time of hearing of the present application for return of the plaint. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the relevant provisions of the Ain as referred to above but those are unnecessary for the primary point in issue in deciding the matter. 

 37. The decision as made herein regarding the claim of the plaintiff upon a prima facie consideration of the material on records, shall not bar the defendant to ask the point to be decided at the final stage of the suit, since the law provides that the question of maintainability goes to the root of the case may be asked and considered after taking evidence in the suit. 

 38. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the relevant provisions of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 as referred above, I am of the opinion that the plaintiffs claim falls under clause (ঠ) of subsection (2) of section 3 and it will come within the ambit of section 4(3) and 4(4) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000.
